correctness.rationale: The count is a bounded martingale, giving A fixation probability x/n. After a near-complete group update, all agents except one or two hold the copied opinion. With one omission the nonabsorbed quotient has subsequent survival rate 2/n. With two omissions, first-step surviving occupancy types have masses u(2,1) and the explicitly counted substochastic 2-by-2 kernel Q satisfies (2,1)Q=lambda(2,1), lambda=(4n-6)/(n(n-1))<1 for n>=4. This proves every-time survival and expectation formulas. Direct labeled-state rational enumeration gave 14,940 matches, independent hypergeometric count transitions 1,575 matches and exact means, and a three-holdout example gave 2/3, 1/2, 59/150 survival probabilities. Finite checks corroborate rather than replace proof.

value.rationale: Exact time-to-consensus distributions and winner probabilities are motivated observables in higher-order voter dynamics. The theorem uses a constant-size rank-one transient quotient to replace numerical matrix inversion for every population and starting opinion split in an infinite complete-hypergraph family, and identifies a concrete three-holdout boundary where the one-rate phenomenon fails. It provides a structural full law, not a trivial parameter substitution or isolated low-order example.
